standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-regularity, H_1-regularity and Koszul-regularity of a sequence, and the equivalences between them for sequences generating the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the author cites Lemma lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular at proof lines 7740-7742
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction of the last two parts to the quasi-regular case.

standard_prerequisites.name: The change-of-basis matrix between two generating sequences induces a map of Koszul complexes which is an isomorphism after inverting its determinant
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the author cites Lemma lemma-functorial at proof lines 7730-7733
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the comparison map between the two Koszul complexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cohomology modules of the Koszul complex of a sequence generating the ideal are annihilated by the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the author cites Lemma lemma-homotopy-koszul at proof lines 7734-7736
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the local isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism over the whole ring.

core_obligations: Assume the ideal is generated by a quasi-regular sequence of minimal length: show that the conormal module is free of rank r and that the given generators form a basis, and deduce that the given sequence is quasi-regular (proof lines 7724-7731).

Write the known quasi-regular generators as linear combinations of the given ones, note that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is a unit modulo the ideal, and compare the two Koszul complexes through the induced map (proof lines 7733-7738).
Use the annihilation of the Koszul cohomology by the ideal to conclude that the comparison map is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 7738-7740).
Reduce the H1-regular and Koszul-regular cases to the quasi-regular one by the equivalence of the notions and repeat the argument (proof lines 7740-7754).
proof_roadmap: Quasi-regular case via the conormal module (proof lines 7724-7731).
Compare the Koszul complexes by the change-of-basis matrix (proof lines 7733-7738).
Upgrade to a quasi-isomorphism using the annihilation (proof lines 7738-7740).
Reduce the other two notions and conclude (proof lines 7740-7755).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the three regularity notions of a sequence depend only on the ideal generated, provided the sequence has the minimal possible length, and the proof is a 32-line argument built on the comparison of Koszul complexes. It first observes that a quasi-regular generating sequence of minimal length has free conormal module, which forces the given generators to form a basis and hence the maps from symmetric powers of the conormal module to be isomorphisms, so the given sequence is quasi-regular; then it compares the two Koszul complexes by a change-of-basis matrix, uses the invertibility of the determinant modulo the ideal and the annihilation of the cohomology by the ideal to upgrade an isomorphism after inverting the determinant to a quasi-isomorphism; finally the H1-regular and Koszul-regular cases are reduced to the quasi-regular one by the equivalence of the notions for such sequences. Each of the three steps uses one named statement of the chapter.
